# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy v2 (16 Nov 2026)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Theory of change
One founder with evenings, weekends, decent writing and okay Python cannot out-research the labs.
But the field has measurement gaps: safety-relevant behaviors and capabilities that nobody is
publicly tracking. Making those gaps visible — and building small, credible evals for the worst
ones — is neglected, tractable at our scale, and useful to funders, researchers, and policymakers
regardless of how the technology unfolds. Morgan's own instinct ("evals for something nobody is
measuring") points here, and the people already offering help (a data analyst, an indie evals
builder) fit it.

## Workstream 1 — The Neglected Measurements Map (primary)
1. Catalogue existing public evals/benchmarks: what each measures, maintainer, freshness.
   (Priya Raman has offered ~5 hrs/wk; this is her first task.)
2. Interview ~10 researchers/practitioners (contacts list) on what they wish were measured.
3. Publish a gap map: ranked list of unmeasured safety-relevant behaviors, with reasoning.
4. Build minimal, open-source evals for the top 1–2 gaps.

Milestones: catalogue v1 by mid-Dec; gap map published by end of Jan; first eval by end of Mar.

## Workstream 2 — Funding
- Emberfall rapid grant (due 30 Nov): $5k–$25k to fund Workstream 1. Draft in
  `docs/emberfall-proposal-draft.md`. Morgan must review, own, and submit — he is the
  accountable applicant.
- Compute Commons rolling credits (computecommons.org) once evals work starts.
- Morgan's own money is a backstop only, capped at $2,000/yr.

## Workstream 3 — Presence (deliberately minimal)
- One unsigned public web page describing the org and the project.
- No press, no open letters, no social posts naming Morgan until HR clearance.
- First real publicity moment = publishing the gap map, not opinions.

## What we are explicitly NOT doing now
- A newsletter (crowded), a reading group (low leverage), policy sign-ons (premature),
  hot takes to journalists (risk to Morgan's employment, zero mission value).

## Risks
- Morgan's Dorrance contract: outside-activities disclosure due 30 Nov; public-statement
  clause unresolved. Mitigation: everything public stays unsigned until cleared.
- Credibility: mitigate by publishing data and code, not opinions.
- Scams/prompt-injection targeting this mailbox (see decisions log).

Halcyon Threshold

Working toward the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Superintelligent AI may be the best thing that ever happens to the world. Whether it is depends on choices being made now — and on knowing things about these systems that, today, nobody is measuring.

Current project: The Neglected Measurements Map

We are building a public map of the measurement gaps in AI safety:

  • Catalogue — an open dataset of existing public evaluations and benchmarks: what each one measures, who maintains it, and how fresh it is.
  • Gap map — a ranked, reasoned list of safety-relevant AI behaviors and capabilities that no one is publicly measuring.
  • Proof of repair — small, open-source evaluations for the most important gaps, to show they can be closed cheaply.

All outputs will be open: data, code, and reasoning. First publications expected winter 2026–27.

Principles

  • Publish measurements and data, not hot takes.
  • Stay small, concrete, and legible.
  • Be useful to researchers, funders, and policymakers whatever the technology does next.

Get involved

If you can help catalogue evaluations, know of a measurement gap that keeps you up at night, or want to fund this work, write to hello@halcyonthreshold.org.

Halcyon Threshold · 2026 · halcyonthreshold.org
